surface_verification.justification: backend classifier change in shipwright-security's scripts/lib (path-string decision functions) plus its test files and a triage-record dismissal; no startable web/dev-server/CLI surface of its own to browser-verify -- verification is the unit test suite itself (F0).

behaviors.behavior: .shipwright/compliance/ paths (incl. the confirmed deploy-gate oracle ci-security.json) are removed from is_safe_to_skip_review entirely, while is_generated_path still hides them from the model

.shipwright/agent_docs/iterates/ paths are removed from is_safe_to_skip_review entirely (not merely re-anchored), across the canonical run-id shape, malformed run_ids, and nested/quarantine paths, while is_generated_path still hides them
.shipwright/agent_docs/runtime/ paths are removed from is_safe_to_skip_review entirely, while is_generated_path still hides them
a CHANGELOG-unreleased.d/ drop in the anchored <category>/<name>_<NNN>.md shape (one of the six real categories, ASCII 3-digit counter) stays safe to skip
a CHANGELOG-unreleased.d/ drop off the anchored shape (wrong category name/case, missing/short/nested counter, or a Unicode-digit counter) is never safe to skip
no review-evidence path (reviews.json, the three internal reply basenames, external-*review* names, self-review-payload.json, mixed-case or off-shape lookalikes) is ever safe to skip, in any shape

the canonical basenames (shipwright_test_results.json, shipwright_events.jsonl, .shipwright/triage.jsonl, .shipwright/triage.outbox.jsonl) stay safe to skip only at their canonical repo-root path, not at an attacker-chosen nested path

review_record_tier.classify_generated_only imports and calls the relocated is_safe_to_skip_review from the new pr_review_skip_safety module (not the old pr_review_generated module) and composes it correctly with the sensitive-path check
is_generated_path's own hide-side behavior (the file-split's other half) is unaffected by the skip-safety changes
